chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn Uthman and Sindi ibn Muhammad, all of them, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about fasting in the month of Sha'ban, and I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, was one of your forefathers (peace be upon them) fasting in Sha'ban?' He said, 'The best of my forefathers is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and most of his fasting was in Sha'ban.'

key_terms.أَكْثَرُ صِيَامِهِ: Most of his fasting / his predominant fasting
key_terms.صَوْمِ شَعْبَانَ: Fasting in the month of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fasting in the month of Sha'ban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) consistent practice of fasting in Sha'ban, a tradition later emulated by the Imams, particularly Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Shaykh al-Tusi includes this in the chapter on Sha'ban fasting to establish it as a recommended (mustahabb) act of worship, linking the Prophet’s devotion to the subsequent Imams' piety. The emphasis on 'most of his fasting' suggests a voluntary, preparatory devotion rather than an obligatory fast, reinforcing the spiritual significance of the month preceding Ramadan.
